north_arrow_measurement.description: Small wheel with an arrow line through it set diagonally on the page, about 63 px long; fitted to the line outside the wheel on both sides. The two sides alone differ by about six degrees at this resolution, hence the large drafting term. Which end is north cannot be read at this resolution; bearings folded to 0-180 do not depend on it.

main_system_reason: The long wall of RGP-4 is the longest measured line at Rangpur and the walls of room 11 agree with it; room 19 in RGP-2 lies close to the same direction relative to its own rose.
notes: We measured two trench plans from Rao's 1963 report, RGP-4 (Fig. 8) and RGP-2 (Fig. 6). Both are reproduced at about 100 dpi and carry only a small wheel-shaped rose with a diagonal arrow line, which dominates the error. On both plans the walls run roughly diagonally to the drawn north, about forty degrees from it, so their folded deviations lie near the plus or minus 45 degree limit. Rooms are labelled with structural phase numbers that we did not map to Rao's Periods IIA-III; some of the measured walls may be Late Harappan. The walls of different phases differ in direction by several degrees, and walls 17 and 18 in RGP-2 are oblique to the rest and were fitted only to the axes of their brick masses. The general contour plan of the site (Plate I) shows no architecture and was not measured.
